    Rigidity of irreducible arrows in a finite ray category #

    Factorization comparability and the absence of nontrivial invertible endorays force two irreducible rays with the same endpoints to coincide. Consequently the neighboring vertex determines an incoming or outgoing quiver arrow.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.rayQuiver_hom_subsingleton {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms C] [IsFiniteRayCategory C] (x y : RayVertex C) :
    Subsingleton (x ⟶ y)

    A finite ray category has no parallel arrows in its reversed irreducible-morphism quiver.
